Exodus 28:17 and 39:10 list it as the second stone in the high priest's breastplate's first row—part of the sacred vestments representing the tribes of Israel. Job compares wisdom's value to precious stones, declaring that even 'the topaz of Cush' cannot equal it (28:19)—Cush (Ethiopia) being famous for gems. Ezekiel includes topaz among the precious stones adorning the king of Tyre in Eden (28:13). The stone's yellow or golden color and rarity made it treasured for sacred and royal ornamentation."
